title: Input Snapshots Fusion for Scalable Discrete-Time Dynamic Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Dynamic graph representation learning models temporal-spatial patterns in real-world applications.

gap.claim: Temporal edges in discrete-time dynamic graphs are underexplored, while existing approaches often incur high computational and memory costs by relying on additional sequential models.

contributions.claim: The authors propose SFDyG, a dynamic graph neural network that combines Hawkes processes with graph neural networks to capture temporal and structural patterns.
SFDyG fuses multiple snapshots into a single temporal graph and decouples computational complexity from the number of snapshots, supporting full-batch and mini-batch training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experimental evaluations on eight diverse dynamic graph datasets for future link prediction.
The authors report that SFDyG consistently outperforms existing methods on the evaluated task and datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dynamic graph representation learning increasingly models temporal-spatial patterns in real-world applications.
Temporal edges in discrete-time dynamic graphs remain underexplored, and sequential-model-based approaches can be computationally and memory intensive for large graphs.
SFDyG combines Hawkes processes with graph neural networks and fuses multiple snapshots into a single temporal graph.
The authors report evaluations on eight diverse datasets for future link prediction and consistent performance improvements over existing methods.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the eight datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture, Hawkes-process formulation, or training complexity in detail.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
